'''Darrun Hilliard II''' (born April 13, 1993) is an American basketball player. The son of Charlene Jenkins and Darrun Hilliard, the younger Hilliard played basketball and football as a youth. He attended [[Liberty High School (Bethlehem, Pennsylvania)|Liberty High School]] in [[Bethlehem, Pennsylvania]], where he was a two-time ''[[Associated Press]]'' first-team selection. As a senior in high school, he averaged 19.7 points per game. Hilliard committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]] and coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]]. He showed steady improvement every year, going from 4.8 points per game as a freshman to 14.3 points per game as a senior as he helped Villanova reach the NCAA Tournament in three straight seasons. As a senior, he was named to the first-team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] and was honored as [[Robert V. Geasey Trophy|Big 5 Player of the Year]].

==Early life==
Hilliard was born on April 13, 1993 to Charlene Jenkins and Darrun Hilliard.<ref name=Villanova>{{cite web|title=4 - Darrun Hilliard|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/darrun_hilliard_760838.html|website=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|publisher=[[Villanova University]]|accessdate=December 23, 2014}}</ref> His mother is a representative for an insurance company.<ref name=Mothers>{{cite news|last1=Smallwood|first1=John|title=Villanova's Hilliard thinks every day should be Mother's Day|url=http://articles.philly.com/2013-05-12/sports/39205730_1_darrun-hilliard-mother-parent-and-child|accessdate=December 23, 2014|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=May 12, 2013}}</ref> His father played basketball at the high school level and first introduced his son to the sport when he was five years old. The younger Hilliard also played football growing up, but preferred basketball.<ref name=ExpressTimes>{{cite news|last1=Hinkel|first1=Tom|title=Liberty High School's Darrun Hilliard repeats as Boys Basketball Player of the Year|url=http://www.lehighvalleylive.com/sports/index.ssf/2011/03/liberty_high_schools_darrun_hi.html|accessdate=December 23, 2014|work=[[The Express-Times]]|date=March 29, 2011}}</ref> His favorite NBA player was [[Allen Iverson]].<ref name=careerday/> He used to bike to Eagles practices as a kid.<ref name=saved>{{cite news|last1=Frank|first1=Reuben|title=Darrun Hilliard on Villanova teammates: 'They saved my life'|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/ncaa/darrun-hilliard-villanova-teammates-they-saved-my-life|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[Comcast SportsNet]]|date=March 23, 2015}}</ref>

==High school career==
Hilliard attended [[Liberty High School (Bethlehem, Pennsylvania)|Liberty High School]] in [[Bethlehem, Pennsylvania]], where he was a two-time ''[[Associated Press]]'' first-team selection.<ref name=Mothers /> Despite eating, writing, and throwing a football right handed, Hilliard shoots left-handed. As a freshman, he measured 6'1. His parents split up after his freshman year, and he developed a unique bond with Liberty assistant coach Mike Bachman.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jones|first1=David|title=Darrun Hilliard is Villanova's hidden engine in its 24-3 season|url=http://www.pennlive.com/sports/index.ssf/2014/02/darrun_hilliard_is_villanovas.html|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[The Patriot-News]]|date=February 24, 2014}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 18 points and six rebounds per game and shot 52 percent from the field. Hilliard led the Hurricanes to [[PIAA]] state semifinals, where Liberty lost to [[Penn Wood High School|Penn Wood]]. In the loss to Penn Wood, Hilliard had 26 points. He was named [[The Morning Call|Morning Call]] player of the year as a junior.<ref name=Groller>{{cite news|last1=Groller|first1=Keith|title=Liberty's Darrun Hilliard is The Morning Call's boys player of the year|url=http://articles.mcall.com/2010-04-02/sports/all-bkbplayerofyear.7224579apr02_1_jersey-shore-warriors-lehigh-valley-conference-tourney-piaa-4a|accessdate=December 23, 2014|work=[[The Morning Call]]|date=April 2, 2010}}</ref> In addition, he was selected to the First Team Class AAAA.<ref>{{cite news|title=Liberty High School's Darrun Hilliard named first team all-state; Chad Landis is Class AAAA co-coach of the year|url=http://www.lehighvalleylive.com/sports/index.ssf/2010/04/post_48.html|accessdate=December 23, 2014|work=[[The Express-Times]]|date=April 7, 2010}}</ref>

Hilliard averaged 19.7 points per game as a senior.<ref name=Villanova /> He was named ''[[Express-Times]]'' player of the year after leading the Hurricanes to the second round of the PIAA playoffs. Hilliard scored 1,413 points in his high school career, finishing second in Liberty history to [[Warren West]].<ref name=ExpressTimes/> He committed to [[Villanova University|Villanova]] in November 2010.<ref name=Emotional>{{cite news|last1=Housenick|first1=Tom|title=It will be an emotional homecoming for Villanova's Darrun Hilliard, a Liberty High product|url=http://touch.mcall.com/#section/-1/article/p2p-81956336/|accessdate=December 23, 2014|work=[[The Morning Call]]|date=November 12, 2014}}</ref> When Hilliard informed his mother he was receiving a full scholarship to Villanova, she did not understand and was trying to figure how much she would have to pay for her son's education.<ref name=Mothers />

==College career==
===Freshman===
Villanova coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] considered [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] Hilliard in his freshman season, but Wright decided against it after a rash of injuries to his players.<ref name=Emotional /> He had 13 points in back-to-back games against [[2011–12 Penn Quakers men's basketball team|Penn]] and [[2011–12 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] in December 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Villanova 73, Penn 65|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313370222|accessdate=June 1, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 3, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Marcus Denmon scores 28 points, leads Missouri at Jimmy V Classic|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313400222|accessdate=June 1, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 7, 2011}}</ref> As a freshman, Hilliard averaged 4.8 points, 2.5 rebounds and 18.1 minutes per game in 29 games and shot 29.2 percent from behind the 3-point arc. During the season, he reached out to his family and friends to see if he made the right decision to come to Villanova. He said, "Freshman year was probably my toughest year of basketball," due to difficulties in adjusting to a new coach and teammates.<ref name=Emotional /> He described himself as a mentally unstable 17-year old.<ref name=saved/>

===Sophomore===
In his sophomore season ([[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]]), he averaged 11.4 points in just under 30 minutes a game. This proved to be his breakout season and he would go on to start all 34 games that year.<ref name=Villanova/> He helped Villanova defeat a few top five teams that season. In a comeback win over #5 [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] on January 22, he made a 3-point play after making a steal at halfcourt which helped spark the rally.<ref>{{cite news|title=Achraf Yacoubou's late 3-pointer helps Nova upset No. 5 Louisville|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330220222|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 23, 2013}}</ref> In a 75–71 overtime victory over #3 [[2012–13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] on January 26, 2013, he had 25 points and six assists in 38 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|title=Villanova uses deep touch to upend No. 3 Syracuse in overtime|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330260222|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 26, 2013}}</ref> As a result of his play against Syracuse, Hilliard was honored as Big East Player of the Week and Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hinkel|first1=Tom|title=Former Liberty High School basketball standout Darrun Hilliard is a rising star at Villanova|url=http://www.lehighvalleylive.com/sports/index.ssf/2013/01/former_liberty_high_basketball.html|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[Express-Times]]|date=January 30, 2013}}</ref> He also helped them beat then #5 [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] on March 6 by the score of 67–57. In that game, he had 14 points, got three [[steal (basketball)|steals]] and made a critical three-pointer with 5:42 left in the second half.<ref>{{cite news|title=Villanova beats another top-5 team, sinks No. 5 Georgetown|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330650222|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 7, 2013}}</ref>

Villanova enjoyed a 20–14 season after a down year and reached the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] where they were seeded ninth and matched up with eight seed [[2012–13 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the first round. Hilliard had a strong showing in a 78–71 loss to [[2012–13 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]], scoring 18 points.<ref>{{cite news|title=UNC outlasts Villanova to give Roy Williams win No. 700|accessdate=March 12, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=March 22, 2013|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330810153}}</ref>

===Junior===
Hilliard improved in most offensive categories in the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]], his junior year. He averaged 14.3 points per game that season and improved his three-point shooting percentage to 41.4 percent (up from 31.5 percent the year before). He made 70 [[3-point field goal|three-pointers]] that year out of 169 attempts.<ref name=Villanova/> Hilliard scored 20 points on 8-of-13 shooting against [[2013–14 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] in a 94–85 victory on January 25, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 4 Villanova holds off Marquette, 94-85 in OT|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400504544|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 25, 2014}}</ref> In an 82–79 win over [[2013–14 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]], he hit a crucial 3-pointer with a minute left in overtime.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 9 Villanova survives scare, escapes Providence in 2OT|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400504575|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 19, 2014}}</ref> In a 73–56 win over Marquette on March 2 at the [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]], he established a new career high with 26 points on 7-of-11 shooting from the field.<ref name=careerday>{{cite news|title=Villanova tops Marquette on Darrun Hilliard's career day|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400504592|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 2, 2014}}</ref>

Villanova compiled a 29–5 record and won the [[Big East]] regular season championship and Battle for Atlantis title despite not being ranked in the preseason.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jerardi|first1=Dick|title=Villanova at a loss in tournament|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/columnists/20140324_Villanova_at_a_loss_in_tournament.html|accessdate=June 3, ===Senior===
{{quote box|width=300px|margin=15px|align=right|qalign=right|bgcolor=#c6dbf7|quote=He is the leader of our team, on and off the court. Defensively he can guard small forwards, guards. He always hits big shots for us. Teams are leaning to him a lot more and he's creating shots for his teammates. The way he's handled everything unselfishly and done everything for the team, he's put winning first ahead of individual accomplishments. I'm thrilled that he's a candidate for player of the year and I'd love for him to get it.|source = — Jay Wright<ref name=inline/>}}

Coming into the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]], Hilliard was named to the Preseason Second Team All-Big East.<ref name=bigeast/> He averaged 14.3 points and 2.8 assists per game as a senior.<ref name=Villanova/> Villanova was ranked in the top ten for most of the season thanks to a balanced offense. Hilliard scored 23 points on December 20 in an overtime victory over [[2014–15 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]], hitting 9-of-17 shots. He hit two free throws to give the Wildcats the first lead of the game in overtime before being kicked in the face and tested for concussion-like symptoms.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 7 Villanova stays undefeated with overtime win over Syracuse|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400587863|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 20, 2014}}</ref> Against [[2014–15 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] on January 25, 2015, he scored 24 points and made 6-of-10 three-pointers in a 71–50 victory at home.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hilliard scores 24 to lead No. 4 Villanova over Creighton|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400588431|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 25, 2015}}</ref> On February 14, in a 78–75 victory over [[2014–15 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]], Hilliard scored a career-high 31 points and also set a career high with 8 three-pointers made out of 13 attempts. He also hit the game-winning three-pointer with 1.2 seconds to play in the game. Eight of his nine field goals in that game were three-pointers, and his eight rebounds were one short of a career-high.<ref>{{cite news|title=Darrun Hilliard hits clutch 3 as No. 6 Villanova rallies by No. 18 Butler|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400588458|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 26, 2015}}</ref> He averaged 18.7 points during a nine-game stretch that included the Butler game.<ref name=inline>{{cite news|last1=Juliano|first1=Joe|title=Hilliard in line for Big East honor|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/20150311_Hilliard_in_line_for_Big_East_honor.html|accessdate=June 3, 2015|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 11, 2015}}</ref>

Hilliard led the Wildcats to a 33–3 season. His final game at Villanova was a 71-68 upset at the hands of [[2014–15 N.C. State Wolfpack men's basketball team|N.C. State]] in the NCAA Tournament Round of 32, despite contributing 27 points. Hilliard finished his Villanova career with 1,511 points, 18th highest in school history; 400 rebounds; and 176 steals.<ref name=saved/> Hilliard was a 2014–15 Men's All-District II Team selection by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|U.S. Basketball Writers Association]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2015/alldistrict150310.html| work=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]]| title=USBWA Names 2014-15 Men's All-District Teams| accessdate=April 26, 2015|date=March 10, 2015}}</ref> The ''[[Sporting News]]'' selected him to be a Second Team All American.<ref>{{cite news|last=Linton|first=Chance|title=Sporting News releases 2014-2015 All-American Team|date=March 9, 2015|work=247sports.com|url=http://247sports.com/Bolt/Sporting-News-releases-2014-2015-All-American-Team-36082417|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WuN7ZYFl|archivedate=March 9, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> Hilliard was one of three players, along with [[LaDontae Henton]] and [[Kris Dunn]], to be named to the All Big East First Team.<ref name=bigeast>{{cite web|title=MBB: All-BIG EAST Teams Announced|url=http://www.bigeast.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030815aaa.html|website=[[Big East Conference]]|accessdate=June 3, 2015|date=March 8, 2015}}</ref> He was named to the First Team All-District V by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nabc.org/awards/all_district/2014-15_NABC_Division_I_All-District_Teams_and_Coaches-2.pdf|title=National Association of Basketball Coaches Announces: 2014-15 Division I All-District Teams and UPS All-District Coaches|accessdate=April 8, 2015|date=March 27, 2015|publisher=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]]}}</ref> He was named [[Robert V. Geasey Trophy|Big 5 Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|last=O'Brien|first=Rick|title=College Basketball: Lower Merion's B.J. Johnson transfers from Syracuse to La Salle|url=http://articles.philly.com/2015-03-25/sports/60443663_1_b-j-johnson-ryan-arcidiacono-bobby-johnson|accessdate=May 25, 2015|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 25, 2015}}</ref> After the season he was invited to the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bodner|first1=Derek|title=NBA draft prospects hope to get noticed at Portsmouth|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/draft/2015/04/10/portsmouth-invitational-traveon-graham-wayne-blackshear-lebryan-nash-darrun-hilliard/25523723/|accessdate=June 6, 2015|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 10, 2015}}</ref>
